articles.title: Less time perfecting the shot, more time living in the moment: Putting the vivo V80 to the test
articles.summary: Editor’s note: This content is sponsored by vivo and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler.

blocks.text: Editor’s note: This content is sponsored by vivo and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.

Our generation has been told countless times that we don’t know how to live in the moment. We’ve been criticized for being too immersed in our phones — more concerned with capturing the perfect moment than enjoying what’s happening right in front of us.

But for a generation of digital natives, the two aren’t necessarily mutually exclusive. We can be fully present in an experience and still want something to remember it by. In fact, our camera rolls have become something of a personal diary — filled with moments that mean a lot to us.
And years later, when these photos resurface, it’s rarely just about remembering what happened, but about how we felt at that particular point in our lives.
So naturally, we’d want a phone that makes doing both easier. Something that makes capturing beautiful moments effortless, without compromising on style or everyday functionality.

Equipped with a ZEISS camera system, AI-powered photography features, and a customizable OriginOS 7 interface, the vivo V80 promises to make taking beautiful photos a little less complicated. So we took it out for a stroll to see just how much easier documenting everyday life could actually get.
At 85mm, the camera captured lovely portraits while keeping some of the surroundings in the frame.
At 100mm, I actually expected the photo to lose some sharpness already, but I was pleasantly surprised by how crisp it still turned out.
We also tested the vivo V80’s zoom capabilities, taking the same photo at 1x, 3x, and 10x while standing in the same spot.
At 1x, we captured the entire street, while 3x brought the buildings closer without losing much detail. Even at 10x, we were surprised by how clearly the architectural details came through.
This could be useful at concerts and live shows, where you want to take good photos or videos despite the distance and often unpredictable stage lighting.
Another feature we had fun experimenting with was the vivo V80’s AI Creative Camera.
Take these photos, for example. An afternoon stroll around Salcedo Village looked like springtime in Japan. It’s obviously not how the place looks in real life — but that’s the fun of it.

blocks.caption: SALCEDO VILLAGE, JAPAN? Trying out ‘Travel’ filters on the vivo V80’s AI Creative Camera feature.

blocks.text: This is a photo we shot using the Top Lighting feature. It’s best for when you want a studio-like look even without professional lighting tools.

We also tried the default 50mm setting of the main camera for a candid shot, and I love how the photo turned out even without posing too much (lol). The colors looked natural and vibrant, with the trees and greenery appearing crisp and detailed even in the wider shot.

Another fun feature of the vivo V80 is the Creative Sticker Collage, which lets you turn your photos into personalized layouts. It’s a nice touch for creatives who want to do a little more with their photos. I tested it out using shots of vivo brand ambassador Anne Curtis from the launch.
Another feature I enjoyed exploring was OriginOS 7’s customizable themes. There are four to choose from: Wiggle, Pet Pals, Glint, and StickIt.

I tried the Pet Pals theme, which gives you an adorable virtual pet right on your lock screen. You can even set its waking times, making it feel like your very own digital Tamagotchi! It’s a playful detail that makes interacting with your phone a lot more fun.

One thing that genuinely surprised me was how fast the vivo V80 charges. I walked into a café with my battery at 0%, plugged it in, and when I checked again just 15 minutes later, it was already at 49%! Honestly, I couldn’t believe it. Its 90W FlashCharge is definitely a feature I’d appreciate on particularly busy days.

The vivo V80’s Starwish Purple variant is particularly pretty in person. Its galaxy-inspired design has a subtle shimmer that changes depending on how the light hits it. It’s perfect for people who love aesthetically pleasing things.
Ready to make the upgrade?
The vivo V80 is available in two variants:

items: 8GB + 128GB for P42,999
8GB + 256GB for P47,999

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Gracioso didn’t say he was paid to make allegations vs Dutertes
articles.summary: The false claim stems from a text card shown in a reaction reel, which cites no credible source

blocks.text: Claim: Dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. admitted that National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag paid him to say he delivered cash to the Duterte family.
Why we fact-checked this: A reaction reel posted on October 27 by the Facebook page “vicshy mix vlog” shows a man pointing at and commenting on an inset quote card.

The card featured photos of Matibag and Gracioso with the text: “Binayaran kasi ako ni NBI Melvin Matibag para mag witness ako nga nagdeliver ako mga pera sa pamilya Duterte, si NBI Melvin Matibag pa nagpatawag sa media; GMA, pasensya sa nagawa ko mali sa pamilya Duterte.”
(NBI’s Melvin Matibag paid me to testify that I delivered money to the Duterte family. Matibag was also the one who called the GMA media; sorry for the wrong I did to the Duterte family.)
The reel’s caption, in Bisaya, reads “Gilaglag nasad (Thrown under the bus again).”
As of writing, the video has over 430,000 views, 18,000 reactions, 1,200 comments, and 5,200 shares.

The facts: No credible report shows Gracioso supposedly admitting that he was paid by Matibag or apologizing to the Duterte family. The quote card cites no interview, affidavit, or news report coming from Gracioso himself or any media outlet.

Gracioso’s public position has been the opposite. In an eight-page affidavit, the former police corporal claimed that he had delivered suitcases filled with millions of pesos to Vice President Sara Duterte, as well as cash delivered to her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, and her brother, Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte. He says he did so on the instruction of former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco, who has admitted to knowing Gracioso but denied the money delivery allegations.
Inquirer reported that Gracioso went to the NBI in June after confiding in Father Flaviano Villanueva about his allegations.

Matibag has said the NBI is not treating the former cop’s claims as established facts and that they are still verifying the allegations. He also said Gracioso could face a perjury complaint if his statements are proven false.

Allegations still under probe: In a press conference on October 6, the Vice President denied Gracioso’s claims, saying that he was motivated by money and personal grievances. The Duterte camp later submitted an affidavit to the NBI addressing Gracioso’s cash delivery allegations.

On October 23, Paolo Duterte filed libel and cyber libel complaints against Matibag, Gracioso, and GMA Network journalists over a September 25 episode of 24 Oras that aired their interviews. GMA Network was the first to publish a report about Gracioso’s affidavit.

On October 29, a second man, identified only as “Chris,” filed an affidavit claiming he dropped off suitcases of cash to Duterte. The Vice President’s camp dismissed the allegation as another “tanim (planted)” witness. Matibag said the NBI would summon him and verify his account.
The cash delivery claims are the latest allegations leveled against the Vice President, who is currently facing an impeachment trial at the Senate. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Thames Water asks creditors for more time to help repay £20bn debt pile
articles.summary:
Troubled utility lobbies for deadline on part of the debt to be extended to March 2028

Thames Water has asked its creditors for more time to pay back billions of pounds in debt, as the water…

blocks.text: Thames Water has asked its creditors for more time to pay back billions of pounds in debt, as the water company scrambles to keep itself afloat.

The UK’s largest water company said it had proposed an “interim” deal under which the deadline to pay off an unspecified portion of the £20bn of debt on its balance sheet would be extended from 2027 to March 2028.

The company, which serves 16 million customers across London and the Thames Valley, has been on the brink of collapse for several years after it became overwhelmed by a huge debt pile. Its shareholders walked away in 2024, which has left the company under the effective control of its creditors, who are working out a deal to avoid bankruptcy.

The creditors gave Thames a separate £3bn lifeline in February last year to try to see it through negotiations on a deal to cut its debts and inject more money. The creditors, collectively called the London & Valley Water company, are led by a group of American hedge funds including Elliott Management and Silver Point Capital, and institutional investors including BlackRock and M&G.

Last month, Thames also asked creditors for a further £2.4bn emergency loan, as it warned it would be unable to reach a longer-term deal to sort out its debt pile before running out of cash by “the end of 2026 or the start of 2027”.

The prime minister, Andy Burnham, faces a decision on whether to allow a takeover deal by the water company’s creditors, which would involve writing off fines and reducing the company’s environmental commitments. He is also mulling whether to nationalise Thames Water or approve another form of state control.
Labour politicians and environmental campaigners have said Burham should instead put Thames Water into special administration, a form of temporary government control while a new buyer is sought.
On Monday, the Liberal Democrats called on Burnham to tell parliament what he is doing to fix the water industry if he does not publish a full plan by the end of the year.
after newsletter promotion

The party’s environment spokesperson, Tim Farron, said Burnham had “talked up water in his conference speech earlier this year, but speeches don’t stop sewage and families paying every higher bills can’t wait years for a 10-year plan to start.”

The industry regulator, Ofwat, recently announced that water companies could increase annual tariffs by an extra £3.4bn, on top of the 36% average rise agreed over five years to 2030. Customer bills are rising to pay for long-overdue investments to fix leaking pipes and treatment works, as well as to pay for new assets such as reservoirs.

Thick fog will shroud much of the southern half of England, the…

blocks.text: Thick fog will shroud much of the southern half of England, the eastern half of Wales and most of Northern Ireland throughout the early part of the week, forecasters have said, as commuters are told to expect delays.
There was disruption to flights at Heathrow airport on Monday, while an incident involving 30 vehicles closed a major road in Kent on Saturday evening.

Niamh Murray, a Met Office operational meteorologist, said current weather conditions were the “perfect recipe” for fog. “With autumn and winter … we get much longer nights, and that allows temperatures to fall away,” she said.

blocks.caption: Fog in Liverpool city centre on Monday. Areas of England south of Manchester have been issued a yellow weather warning. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

blocks.text: “We get a longer period of cooling and also the temperatures are much lower, so they’re much closer to the temperature that we need for the air to become saturated and therefore form fog.

“Another thing that we need to form fog is quite light winds, not absolutely no winds. We just have the perfect recipe at the moment – light winds, clear skies, long nights – to allow that fog to develop. And particularly if we see the negative numbers [the temperature in degrees Celsius], it can be quite stubborn to clear the next day.”

Forecasters issued yellow weather warnings, the least severe, for Monday in areas covering: most of England south of Manchester, with the exception of Devon and Cornwall; eastern parts of Wales, including Cardiff; and most of Northern Ireland, with the exception of Belfast. Visibility could be down to 50 metres or less in some places, with delays to bus and train services possible and a chance of flight cancellations.

blocks.caption: Dense fog on Wimbledon Common, London, on Saturday. Photograph: Amer Ghazzal/Shutterstock

blocks.text: The affected area is likely to shrink to the Midlands, Staffordshire and Cheshire in the west of England on Tuesday, and eastwards across most of Yorkshire, Lincolnshire and East Anglia.

On Monday morning, a spokesperson for Heathrow said: “Overnight fog has affected visibility on roads around Heathrow and conditions may continue into this morning. If you’re travelling to the airport, please allow extra time for your journey. We advise passengers to check with their airline before leaving home and to drive with care.”
An 30-vehicle incident in foggy conditions on Saturday left two people seriously injured and closed the M20 in Kent between junction eight and nine near Maidstone.

blocks.caption: Drivers have been warned to lower their speed to avoid collisions amid the thick fog. Photograph: Geoffrey Swaine/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Edmund King, president of the AA, previously said: “Fog can transform a familiar road in a matter of minutes, so drivers need to be prepared to adapt their speed and leave more room between themselves and the vehicle ahead.

“One of the biggest mistakes is simply following the rear lights of the car in front. It can give you a false sense of security and means you may be travelling too close to react safely if that vehicle suddenly stops. Ultimately, there’s no prize for arriving a few minutes early. Give yourself extra time, slow down and drive to what you can actually see ahead.”

articles.title: Who will get new laptops? Here’s how DepEd will decide
articles.summary: More than 200 MacBook Neo laptops are turned over to 10 public schools in Dagupan City on Monday, November 9

blocks.text: MACBOOK NEO. The Department of Education starts the distribution of over 230,000 laptops, mostly MacBook Neo units, to public school teachers and administrative officers in Dagupan City, Pangasinan, on November 9, 2026.
Department of Education
More than 200 MacBook Neo laptops are turned over to 10 public schools in Dagupan City on Monday, November 9

items: The Department of Education has begun distributing over 230,000 laptops to public school teachers, starting with 209 MacBook Neo units in Dagupan City, Pangasinan.
The distribution prioritizes teachers without government-issued laptops, focusing on those with the greatest need and evaluating their access to technology and teaching responsibilities.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Education (DepEd) has started the distribution of over 230,000 laptops to public school teachers and administrative officers.
For the first batch, the DepEd turned over 209 MacBook Neo laptops to public school teachers and administrative officers across 10 schools in Dagupan City, Pangasinan, on Monday, November 9.

Among the recipients was Dagupan City National High School, which got 72 MacBook Neo units — a huge jump from the four official laptops it had for teachers. The school has 312 personnel, serving around 5,000 high school students.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos attended the turnover ceremony.
“I know many of you bought your own, used your own salary, just to do the work that you have to do. That should not be your burden anymore,” Marcos told teachers in a speech.

blocks.caption: TURNOVER. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. leads the turnover of laptops under the DepEd Computerization Program at Dagupan City National High School in Pangasinan on November 9, 2026. Photo from Presidential Communications Office

blocks.text: The latest batch of procured laptops under the DepEd Computerization Program includes 172,654 MacBook Neo units and 62,717 Windows-based units. The MacBooks will be distributed until March 2027.
According to the education department, it procured and delivered 140,430 laptops for teachers from 2022 to 2025.
With around 900,000 public school teachers in the country, here’s how the DepEd will decide who will receive new laptops:
The distribution focuses on schools that have not previously received teacher laptops through the DepEd Computerization Program, other government programs, local government units, or donors.
For the latest batch of laptops, qualified teachers must have the following:

items: An active teaching assignment
An active DepEd email with multi-factor authentication enabled
No working laptop issued by the government or school and received between January 1, 2023 and November 6, 2026

blocks.text: The education department clarified that having shared equipment or a personally bought laptop will not disqualify a teacher.

“Selection within each school strictly prioritizes teachers with the greatest need for a functional device by evaluating their existing access to gadgets, teaching responsibilities, and digital readiness consistently and fairly,” the agency said.

If eligible teachers exceed available units, the first priority will be teachers without a government-issued laptop who “actively lead educational technology efforts, such as ICT (information and communications technology) coordinators, EdTech champions, or Khan Academy teachers.”
The second priority would be all other eligible teachers without a government-issued laptop.
The third priority category consists of teachers who were previous laptop recipients, but their units have been declared unserviceable, destroyed by calamities, or lost to theft or robbery.

“Seniority and non-teaching duties do not grant priority. If a priority group exceeds remaining units, schools must conduct a witnessed drawing of lots manually or through the Teacher Assignment for Laptop Allocation (TALA) system,” the DepEd said.
The TALA system is the education department’s new registration app for device inventory and property management.

blocks.caption: NEW LAPTOPS. Teachers of Dagupan City National High School in Pangasinan try out their MacBook Neo units on November 9, 2026. Photo from Presidential Communications Office

blocks.text: School heads must review teacher assignments and individual laptop issuance history. This must be coordinated with the school property custodian.
The finalized list, which includes recipients and ranked alternates, must be encoded into the TALA system by Sunday, November 15.
The DepEd reminded recipient schools that laptops remain government property.

“Teachers promoted or reassigned outside the teaching track must surrender their devices for reallocation. Units will be enrolled in DepEd’s Mobile Device Management system, and unauthorized sales or transfers are strictly prohibited,” it said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: In a first, Japan’s security aid to Philippines includes defense equipment
articles.summary: Japan will provide the Philippines with a coastal radar system and surveillance drones under a ¥4.3-billion security grant.

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 6:19pm
A mobile air-surveillance radar system delivered to the Philippine Air Force in March 2024 is shown in this photo released April 30, 2024.
Mitsubishi Electric / Released

MANILA, Philippines — Japan will supply the Philippines with a coastal radar system and surveillance drones under a ¥4.3-billion grant (roughly P1.72 billion) signed in Manila on Monday, November 9, the first transfer of finished defense equipment through Tokyo's security aid program.

Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro and Japanese Ambassador Kitagawa Katsuro signed and exchanged diplomatic notes for the fiscal 2026 package under Japan's Official Security Assistance (OSA), a grant program that funds equipment and facilities for the armed forces of Tokyo's partner countries.
The two officials also signed notes for a separate grant to improve the water supply system of Cotabato City.

Japan has provided coastal radars to the Philippine Navy under OSA before. But the package signed Monday involves a radar system that Japan classifies as "defense equipment," its first such transfer through its security aid program since its launch in 2023.

"This project includes the first defense equipment transfer under Japan’s OSA program which aims to provide a coastal radar system, classified as defense equipment, to the Philippine Navy, and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) for monitoring and surveillance to the Philippine Air Force," Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a release.

The ministry said the radar and the unmanned aerial vehicles would strengthen the Armed Forces of the Philippines' (AFP) maritime domain awareness and surveillance capabilities. Simply put, this refers to the military's ability to see what ships and aircraft are moving through Philippine waters and airspace.

Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro and Japanese Ambassador Kitagawa Katsuro signs and exchanges diplomatic notes for the fiscal 2026 package under Japan's Official Security Assistance (OSA), Nov. 9, 2026.
Japan Ministry of Foreign Affairs
First island chain

Japan and the Philippines both sit on the so-called first island chain, the string of islands running from Japan through Taiwan to the Philippines that separates China's coastal seas from the western Pacific.
The Luzon Strait, between Taiwan and northern Luzon, is one of the main sea passages linking the South China Sea to the Pacific.

Japan's foreign ministry said the Philippines faces important sea lanes, including the South China Sea and the Luzon Strait, and plays an important role in regional security. The project would make sea lanes important to Japan more secure and help maintain regional peace and stability, it added.

"This reaffirms our shared commitment in enhancing Philippine defense capability and in advancing initiatives that support communities in Mindanao," Lazaro said in a post on X, calling the signing a concrete demonstration of the two countries' Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
Under the first OSA grant to the Philippines, signed in November 2023, five coastal radar systems reached the country in January 2026 and were formally handed over a month later.

articles.title: Greek authorities find 12 bodies in a boat carrying migrants south of Crete; 18 people rescued
articles.summary: Greece is one of the main entry points into the European Union for people fleeing conflict and poverty in the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

image.caption: FILE PHOTO - Frontex, foreground, and Greek coast guard vessels take part in a search and rescue operation, after the capsizing of a boat carrying migrants, off the coast on the northeastern Aegean Sea island of Lesbos, Greece, on April 3, 2025. (Panagiotis Balaskas/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
Greece is one of the main entry points into the European Union for people fleeing conflict and poverty in the Middle East, Africa and Asia.
No further information was immediately available on the identities of the 12 people who died

Greek authorities recovered 12 bodies from a boat carrying migrants found sailing south of Greece's island of Crete early Monday, while a passing Moroccan-flagged cargo ship rescued 18 people from the same vessel, the coast guard said.

No further information was immediately available on the identities of the 12 people who died, or the circumstances of their deaths. Greece's coast guard said the boat they were travelling in was found about 15 nautical miles - about 28 kilometres - south of the southern Mediterranean island of Crete on Monday morning.

Another two boats, one carrying about 47 people and another with about 40 people on board, were also found sailing south of Crete. The first was spotted by an aircraft from the European Union's border agency Frontex , while the second was found by a Frontex drone, the coast guard said.
The agency added that those on board both boats were rescued by Frontex and were being taken to a port on the southern coast of Crete.

Greece is one of the main entry points into the European Union for people fleeing conflict and poverty in the Middle East, Africa and Asia. In recent months, thousands have been making the perilous sea crossing from north Africa, usually from Libya to Crete . Others make the far shorter but often equally dangerous crossing from the Turkish coast to nearby Greek islands in the Aegean Sea, often in unseaworthy inflatable dinghies or other small boats.
Last month, 12 people, including an infant, died when the two boats they were traveling in from Turkey to the islands of Lesbos and Samos capsized.

Frontex said in October that the eastern Mediterranean was the busiest route for migrants attempting to enter the 27-nation EU, although irregular border crossings into the bloc were down by a third so far this year.

The agency said that around 31, 800 crossings were recorded in the first three quarters of 2026, a fall of 15% compared with the same period last year. The corridor from Libya to Crete was the busiest section on the route, ahead of the eastern Aegean islands and the land border with Turkey.

articles.title: Pangilinan, De Lima still hopeful Robedo will seek presidency anew in 2028
articles.summary: Allies of former Vice President Leni Robredo remain hopeful that she will change her mind about a second presidential run in 2028.

blocks.text: Published November 9, 2026 6:11pm
Allies of former Vice President Leni Robredo remain hopeful that she will change her mind about a second presidential run in 2028.

On Monday, House Senior Deputy Minority Leader Leila de Lima of ML party-list and and Senator Francis Pangilinan made the comments after Robredo said earlier in the day that she won’t pursue a 2028 presidential bid but would rather support a deserving presidential candidate.

“I find it very regrettable to hear that it is as if she has made up her mind. But you know, hope runs eternal. We continue to hope….we continue to hope na baka naman may [that there is still a] chance pa na magbago ang isip niya [that she will change her mind],” De Lima told reporters.

“Whatever her final decision we're going to respect that. But we're still keeping our fingers crossed. We're still hoping that she will change her mind. We in the LP are yet to talk about this but I am sure that we share the same sentiments [of wanting her to run]. Umaasa talaga akong magbabago ang kanyang desisyon [I am really hoping she will change her decision]. She is the best hope for our country,” De Lima added.

De Lima said that with the filing of candidacy set around last week of September to first week of October next year, Robredo can still reopen that door to a second presidential run and make a decision by first quarter of January 2028.

“Ayaw ko maniwala na talagang tuldok na tuldok na iyong pagkakasara [ng pinto]…ng kanyang desisyon. Personally, ayaw kong tanggapin pa yan at this point. Because I do believe na kailangan talaga siya ng bansa,” she said.
[I don't want to believe that she has closed the door. Personally, I don't want to believe that at this point. I do believe our country needs her.]

“With all of the problems, with all of the issues, with all of the challenges in our country and our political climate is facing right now…ang kailangan natin na somebody like VP Leni. She has proven competence and integrity to implement good governance,” she added.
Robredo ran for president in 2022 but lost against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Robredo got 14 million votes as against Marcos' 31 million.

Senator Pangilinan, for his part, harked back to 26 years when then-Senator Benigno Aquino III also had no plans to run for president but later on went on to be the standard bearer of the opposition for the 2010 polls.
Aquino eventually won the 2010 presidential polls.

“Si dating Pangulong Noynoy nung senador pa sya ay wala ring planong tumakbong presidente. Tinutulan din nya yung unang panawagan ng taumbayn na tumakbo siya sa 2010 pero sa huling banda hindi na siya maka hindi dahil taumbayan na ang nagpasiya at nagsabi na dapat siya tumakbo,” Pangilinan said.
(President Noynoy also had no plans to run for President and turned down offers for him to run. But ultimately, he cannot refuse the call of the people who wanted him to be president.)
“Sa 2028, naniniwala ako na taumbayan din ang magpapasiya at magtatagumpay para sa bayan,” he added.
(For 2028, I am also of the belief that the people’s will is the ultimate decider.) — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Sara witness admits China trip with Davao officials after grilling
articles.summary: Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin faced scrutiny over conflicting statements at trial Monday.

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 6:04pm
Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Nov. 9, 2026.
Senate PRIB

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte's first defense witness admitted Monday, November 9 that he traveled to China with several Davao City officials in January 2026, after senator-judges confronted him with travel records.
Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin confirmed that the city engineer, city treasurer and a city administrator joined the trip, for which they had obtained official travel authorities.

Senator-judges Raffy Tulfo and Risa Hontiveros had challenged Adalin's recollection of his overseas travels. Kiko Pangilinan separately questioned inconsistencies in his testimony about properties linked to Duterte's Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).
Prosecution counsel Benjamin Tolosa had described the China visit as an "all-expense-paid trip."
Adalin initially struggled to recall details of his travels, prompting Tulfo to read from his travel records.
"Jan. 25, 2026, saan ka bumiyahe?" Tulfo asked. ("Where did you travel on Jan. 25, 2026?")
"Indeed, nag-travel po kami sa China," Adalin replied. ("Indeed, we traveled to China.")
Tulfo also cited Adalin's other foreign trips, including a November 2018 visit to China and travels to Hong Kong, Thailand and Australia.
He questioned how Adalin, who earns around P120,000 a month as a local government department head, could afford frequent overseas travel, including a 2023 trip to Australia with a relative.
Adalin maintained that his travels were funded with "personal money," but could not recall the travel agency that arranged the group's bookings.
"Yan ka na naman nagkakaroon ka ng amnesia," Tulfo said. ("There you go again, having amnesia.")
Hontiveros also confronted Adalin with flight records and questioned how a city assessor familiar with complex property maps could not remember where he had traveled in China just 10 months ago.
Adalin attributed his poor recollection to not being "keen on traveling."
Under Hontiveros' questioning, he confirmed that other Davao City officials accompanied him on the January 2026 trip but denied that Duterte was among them.
Inconsistencies in property testimony
Pangilinan separately questioned Adalin's credibility after the witness gave differing answers about a property linked to Duterte's SALN.
"Just just a observation that clearly there are inconsistencies in your testimony. Forgive me, engineer but you say one thing and then you say another thing," Pangilinan said.
"So we are wondering ano ba talaga ang totoo sa sinasabi mo?" he added. ("So we are wondering, what is really true about what you're saying?")
Adalin initially said with certainty that a property covered by a transfer certificate of title ending in 0775 was the same residential lot declared in Duterte's SALN.
But when confronted with street-view photographs showing Prime Bistro operating at the property, Adalin said he was "not sure" whether it was the same site.
After the lunch break, Adalin said he had verified the property with his staff and could now confirm that it was the same lot.

Adalin was called as the defense's first witness to testify about property records relevant to Article II of the Articles of Impeachment, which includes allegations that Duterte failed to fully disclose her assets and liabilities.

articles.title: [Rappler’s Best] Who’s coming to town?
articles.summary: 'The ASEAN Summit and Related Summits could not have come at a more unique moment for the world'

blocks.text: The victor, the vanquished, and the middle power strategist are among the top guns visiting Manila for the 49th Leaders’ Summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), which the Philippine government is hosting next week from November 15 to 18. Check the list of rescheduled and canceled flights affected by the event.
And here’s a bonus: Angelina Jolie is speaking at the 2026 ASEAN Inclusive Growth Summit in Manila on Wednesday, November 11. Read more.
The ASEAN Summit and Related Summits could not have come at a more unique moment for the world.

items: A bruising midterm elections defeat for US President Donald Trump and the MAGA movement he inspired has left countries he has punished with tariffs and wars wondering what he would do next. (For starters, he named the hardliner Stephen Miller his new chief of staff.) Trump will be attending the ASEAN Summit, nearly a decade after he first visited the Philippines during his first presidential term for the 31st ASEAN Summit in 2017, which Manila also hosted.

Brazil President Lula da Silva, fresh from an astounding reelection to a fourth term that stemmed the march of the far right in Latin America, will also be attending the summit upon the invitation of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. — his first visit to Manila as both countries commemorate 80 years of diplomatic ties. Lula defeated Trump’s right-wing ally Flavio Bolsonaro, who fled to the US on claims he was cheated.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, whose Davos speech taking potshots at Trump earned him a standing ovation, is also joining the summit. He had said that the rules-based global order was over and that middle powers must come together, a view echoed by Marcos in 2024 at the Shangri-La Dialogue. Marites Vitug writes how Canada, slapped with heavy tariffs by the US, is finally out of America’s shadow.

blocks.text: China naturally weighs heavily in these meetings, given the elusive Code of Conduct for the South China Sea which ASEAN has been negotiating with Beijing for over two decades now. At the ASEAN Summit last year, then-foreign secretary Enrique Manalo said it was time for the talks to progress and tackle the thorny issues that had been avoided for years. But there’s little doubt that the negotiations will continue to drag.

items: The Code remains to be ASEAN’s North Star, however. Chinese Premier Li Qiang will be participating in the summit. Ahead of the event, Philippine Foreign Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said she had a “frank, pragmatic, and constructive” phone call with her counterpart, Foreign Minister Wang Yi, to discuss “the state of bilateral ties at length.”
In July, both countries held their first foreign minister-level meeting in two years, where Lazaro raised a long list of Manila’s grievances and concerns against Beijing.

The heightened tensions were put in the spotlight in last month’s ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting that was chaired by Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr., and which Chinese Defense Minister Dong Jun skipped.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth also held an informal meeting with the defense chiefs, where he called for “strong, self-reliant” nations in the region. With the Republicans’ defeat and the unpopularity of the Iran war among Americans, the fate of Hegseth is now up in the air.

blocks.text: And how about the rumored signing of the US-backed Pax Silica zone during the summit? No such thing, said the US ambassador to Manila in a statement.

Another major event is happening within the vicinity of the Philippine International Convention Center, where the leaders’ summit and related summits will be held: the resumption of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. It’s the defense panel’s turn to present their evidence.

items: Who are the initial witnesses for the Vice President? Read here.
Duterte’s lawyers initially wanted to present former law dean Ralph Sarmiento as one of their first witnesses, but he declined. Read more about it here.
Dwight de Leon shows us the list of evidence against Duterte that was submitted by the prosecution to the Senate impeachment court.

articles.title: PH to press wealthy nations for climate funding
articles.summary: The Philippines will push for stronger international partnerships and increased climate financing to address the economic impact of extreme weather events, including extreme heat, typhoons and…

blocks.text: COP 31
Published November 9, 2026 5:58pm

The Philippines will push for stronger international partnerships and increased climate financing to address the economic impact of extreme weather events, including extreme heat, typhoons and flooding, at the ongoing UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.

“For millions of Filipino families, climate change is not a distant policy debate — it is an everyday reality affecting their livelihoods, homes, and safety,” Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said in a statement.
The DENR said the economic cost of climate inaction in the Philippines could reach P645 billion annually in the 2030s.
At COP31, Cuna said the Philippines would reaffirm its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 75% by 2035.

The country is also seeking a four- to five-year extension of the Sharm el-Sheikh Mitigation Work Programme to strengthen the link between emissions reduction targets, climate financing and technology transfer, the DENR said.

The Philippines will also push for grant-based funding to support the implementation of its National Adaptation Plan (NAP) and Adaptation Investment Platform, without adding to the debt burden of developing countries.
The government will further seek to ensure that all emissions reductions achieved in the country are credited toward its national climate targets.
It will also call for simplified procedures and direct access to the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage to ensure that disaster-stricken communities benefit from climate assistance.

“As we head into COP31, the Philippines is working towards building constructive international partnerships that back ambitious climate pledges with predictable, accessible financial and technical support so that local communities receive the protection they urgently need,” Cuna said.

However, environmental groups have questioned the government's climate commitments, citing its continued reliance on coal and fossil gas, support for waste-to-energy projects and other policies they said undermine environmental protection.

The Climate Action Tracker has warned that existing Philippine policies could allow emissions to continue rising through 2030, while the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) has called for stronger measures to reduce emissions.

Environmental organizations have also raised concerns about Cuna's environmental track record, including his involvement in the Canadian garbage controversy, although criminal charges against him were dismissed in 2021.
They have urged the DENR to prioritize renewable energy, ecosystem protection and stronger environmental safeguards alongside its push for international climate financing.— MCG, GMA News
Follow GMA News Online on Facebook for real-time news and developments in the Philippines and around the world.

articles.title: Sara Duterte urges government to prepare food supply amid El Niño
articles.summary: The government should prepare the country's food supply and not just urge Filipinos to ready their buckets in response to the impacts of the very strong El Niño phenomenon, Vice President Sara…

blocks.text: Published November 9, 2026 5:57pm

The government should prepare the country's food supply and not just urge Filipinos to ready their buckets in response to the impacts of the very strong El Niño phenomenon, Vice President Sara Duterte said.

"Ang warning ng mga experts sa El Niño ay hindi pangkaraniwan. Sinasabi nila na meron talagang punto na aabot sa drought… Kahit ilan pang balde ang ihanda mo dyan, hindi yan makakatulong," Duterte said during a gathering with overseas Filipino workers in Hong Kong over the weekend.
(The experts warned that this El Niño would be extraordinary. They say we will experience drought... No matter how many more buckets you prepare, it won't help.=

"Ang kailangan paghandaan ng pamahalaan ay kung ano ang supply ng pagkain pagdating ng panahon na 'yan kasi ibig sabihin, pag nasira yung ating ani, mag-import tayo," she added. "Kailangan paghandaan yun ng pamahalaan na hindi lang balde-balde."

(What the government needs to prepare for is the food supply when El Niño hits, because that means if our harvest is affected, we will have to import. The government needs to prepare for that, not just bucket by bucket.)
GMA News Online has reached out to Malacañang for comment on the matter.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. had urged Filipinos to collect rainwater amid the ongoing El Niño phenomenon. To collect rainwater, Marcos said people need to buy buckets.
Malacañang defended the President and explained it is part of rain collection and water purification, one of the government’s responses to the El Niño phenomenon.
The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) then said it was preparing to distribute free water filtration devices, promising to teach communities how to use them.

According to PAGASA, the El Niño phenomenon from the latter part of 2026 to the first half of 2027 is expected to be record-breaking in terms of heat, with temperatures across the Philippines expected to rise by 2C.

“Most climate models predict that the ongoing El Niño will persist until the first quarter of 2027, with its peak expected before the end of 2026. And its associated impacts may continue through the first half of 2027,” PAGASA Climate Monitoring and Prediction Section Chief Ana Liza Solis said.

Department of Science and Technology (DOST) Secretary Renato Solidum Jr. had said that there was no need to hoard water amid the El Niño phenomenon as supply remains sufficient in the next several months.
He urged the public to save rainwater and use it for household needs like washing the car and watering the plants.
The World Food Programme said there is food security when "people have access to enough safe and nutritious food for normal growth and development."
The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has called for soil assessment in the country's farmlands to ensure food security amid the El Niño.

"There may not be rain, but if our groundwater is really secure and it's available, then farmers would be able to produce food," said Dulce Carandang, FAO Philippines assistant representative for the programme. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Russell Brand to be sentenced for rape and sexual assault today – latest updates
articles.summary:
Disgraced comedian was convicted last week and was warned he faces a ‘signficant’ prison term

Following his conviction last week, the Met Police revealed that they were investigating further…

blocks.text: Brand to be sentenced for rape and sexual assault today

blocks.caption: Frances Mao

blocks.text: Frances Mao
Good morning. Russell Brand will be sentenced today after being found guilty of raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others in seperate incidents between 2005-2009.
The disgraced former comedian and Hollywood star has been behind bars since he was convicted by a jury last Thursday, denied bail by his trial judge who ruled that he posed a flight risk.

During the four-week trial, prosecutors had argued that Brand was a ruthless, calculating, manipulative “sexual predator” who pursued women relentlessly and exploited his fame and power to get what he wanted from them sexually.
The 51-year-old father of three is now facing a “significant” prison term, Justice Joel Bennathan said last week.
The sentencing is taking place in Southwark Crown Court in London and commences at 10:30am GMT. I’ll bring you all the developments.
Key events

items: 7m agoBrand could face further charges
8m agoBrand arrives in prison van for sentencing
14m agoBrand denied bail after conviction
16m agoBrand's convictions
23m agoBrand to be sentenced for rape and sexual assault today

blocks.text: Brand could face further charges
Following his conviction last week, the Met Police revealed that they were investigating further rape allegations against Brand, including one involving a then 16-year-old girl.
The Met said they had already questioned Brand on further complaints from two other women, and have submitted the files to crown prosecutors.
The lead detective in the case, Det Supt Andy Furphy, told the Guardian last week he believed there could be more victims.

double quotation markIf you get a conviction then it tends to encourage other people to come forward because they see the courage and the bravery and the resilience that these women have had to go through this criminal justice process, and they feel their own strength as a result of that. They want to come forward and have their story told.

The Met’s investigation into Brand, named Operation Actinolite, involved tracing and speaking to more than 100 witnesses, reviewing more than 1,400 documents and taking more than 340 statements, including from Brand’s former employers, colleagues and associates.
Brand has also been accused of sexually assaulting a woman at his mansion in Los Angeles in 2008, in a civil claim filed at the high court in London.
Brand arrives in prison van for sentencing
The former actor-comedian was transported to Southwark Crown Court in a white prison van. He was held at HMP Wandsworth on the weekend.

blocks.caption: Russell Brand arrives in security van at Southwark Crown Court Photograph: James Veysey/Shutterstock

blocks.text: His wife, Laura Brand, who has been a steadfast and loyal supporter by his side, has also just entered the court. She gave testimony on his behalf, attesting to his good character during the trial.
The couple have three young children together.

blocks.caption: Laura Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court as her husband Russell Brand is due to be sentenced for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three more. Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters
Photograph: Corey Rudy/Reuters

blocks.text: Brand denied bail after conviction

blocks.caption: Russell Brand outside Southwark Crown Court, London last week on Wednesday, 4 November 2026, as he awaited a jury’s decision. Photograph: James Manning/PA

blocks.text: The actor-comedian had been free but was taken into custody immediately after the jury returned the guilty verdicts last Thursday.
His defence lawyer Ian Winter KC had put in a plea for bail, arguing for Brand to have the weekend to say goodbye to his wife and three children.
But this was rejected by Justice Bennathan on the grounds that Brand, with his money and connections, posed a flight risk.
There were substantial grounds to “fear he might in the end not feel able to come along and face his sentence”, the judge said.
double quotation markI regret the hardship caused to the children, of course. But the hardship has been caused by serious criminal offending by their father.

Sitting in the courtroom last week, Brand had closed his eyes when the guilty verdict for the rape charge was read out. After his bail was denied, he gestured OK to his lawyers and repeated “I’m good, I’m good, I’m good”, before being taken away by guards.
Brand's convictions
The jury of eight men and four women deliberated for more than eight hours last week to return a unanimous verdict where they found Brand guilty on four of the seven charges.
He was found guilty of one count of rape and three incidents of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one attempted incident.
Brand had pleaded not guilty to all the offences, telling the court he believed he never had non-consensual sex.

But the jury found he had committed crimes against four women between 2004-2009 in different locations, in a central London bar, a radio station, recording studio and his former home in Hampstead, London.

items: He was convicted of sexually assaulting a woman at a colleague’s birthday party in a bar in Soho, London in 2004, but found not guilty of orally raping her in a bathroom.
He was found guilty of kissing and groping another woman at a London radio station in 2004 or 2005
He was convicted of anally raping a fan at his home after meeting her backstage at one of his comedy shows in 2009
He was found guilty of sexually assaulting a woman who says the comedian demanded a massage and pressed his face into her groin during an advert recording in 2009.

blocks.text: He was acquitted of raping another woman in a hotel room during the Labour Party annual conference in Bournemouth in 1999, and of attempting to indecently assault a woman by dragging her into the bathrooms in the London offices of MTV music channel.

articles.summary:
Louise Haigh is expected to agree to cut a target for EV sales by about a quarter

Here is an article by Fiona Harvey and Jasper Jolly published last month…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 5m agoGovernment promises stronger modern slavery protections for goods sold in UK
15m agoFiona Harvey and Jasper Jolly on impact of cutting EV targets
33m agoPolanski says Labour has ‘shocking record’ on climate issues as ministers expected to cut EV targets for car industry

blocks.text: Government promises stronger modern slavery protections for goods sold in UK

Businesses which trade goods made with slave labour will have to withdraw them from sale, the government has said, revealing it will change the law to enforce the new ban. The Press Association reports:

double quotation markJonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, said he plans to introduce new legislation to introduce mandatory human rights due diligence for companies, which will require them to remove products made with forced labour and modern slavery. He outlined the move in a letter to the Commons business committee, which has been calling for new business safeguards against modern slavery for nearly two years. The new duty will apply to British businesses with a global turnover of more than £350m, and non-UK businesses with a UK-generated turnover of more than £350m. Those who do not comply with the new duty may be forced to withdraw products from sale which have come from forced labour or modern slavery, Reynolds said. The commitee has been calling for modern slavery protections to be strengthened since it heard evidence from Chinese-owned clothing company Shein in January 2025. In that session, the firm repeatedly declined to confirm whether its products contained cotton sourced from China, including Xinjiang, where it is believed that the Uyghur minority are subject to forced labour.
Fiona Harvey and Jasper Jolly on impact of cutting EV targets

Here is an article by Fiona Harvey and Jasper Jolly published last month on what the consequences would be if the government were to relax its EV targets, as the Guardian today reports now seems inevitable. (See 9.26am.)
And here is an extract.

double quotation markThe end goal of 2035 is likely to remain, but under a consultation that ended on Friday, the 2030 targets could be weakened to 70% or even as low as 50% of new cars. Taken with previous watering down of the policy to allow more sales of hybrid cars – which use both electric and combustion engines – that change would lead to emissions greater than burning all the gas in the Jackdaw field, according to the ECIU [Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit]. If the mandate were cut more drastically to require only 50% of sales to be EVs by 2030, this could mean an additional 147 megatonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, which would equate to about 58% of the likely emissions from burning the oil produced by the Rosebank field. Jess Ralston, an analyst at the ECIU, said weakening the target would not solve the problems for manufacturers, who are already facing intensified competition from China as increasing numbers of people opt for EVs. It would also not benefit the public because EVs can be £1,750 a year cheaper to run, and potentially more with oil prices rising.
Polanski says Labour has ‘shocking record’ on climate issues as ministers expected to cut EV targets for car industry

Good morning. Monday is often the busiest day of the week at Westminster but, with the Commons still enjoying a mini November recess, today is looking a bit quiet. Andy Burnham is on a visit to a hospital this morning and he wants to talk about a £40m programme in England to try to keep vulnerable patients out of hospital. The Department of Health and Social Care has the details here, and Andrew Gregory explains it all here.
But Burnham may find he ends up taking more questions from the media on another Guardian story, Kiran Stacey’s scoop about the government being on course to water down electric vehicle (EV) targets.

blocks.caption: Guardian splash. Photograph: Guardian

blocks.text: With Burnham attending the Cop climate crisis summit later this week, the revelations won’t boost Burnham’s credentials with environmentalists.
The final EV decision has not yet been taken, but the Greens are already outraged. These are from Zack Polanski, the Green party leader.

double quotation markThis week leaders meet for the UN climate summit. The context? A summer of heat deaths. Scientists saying 2026 will be the hottest year ever. Our Government’s contribution? To bend over backwards to the car industry, and scrap plans for rapid electrification.

double quotation markThis Government is building up a shocking record of backsliding and bad decisions on climate issues. At a time when we desperately need leadership, they bend to the will of polluters by slashing key rules and pushing ahead with fossil fuel extraction.
And this is from the former Green leader Caroline Lucas.

double quotation markA truly terrible decision at a truly terrible time. The shift to electric vehicles is government’s single biggest decarbonisation policy. Cutting EV targets would send a message on eve of #COP31 that UK is no longer serious about #climate action.
Here is the agenda for the day.
Morning: Andy Burnham is visiting a hospital in Hertfordshire.
11.30am: Downing Street holds a lobby briefing.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: AI image falsely shows Army division backing Bato dela Rosa
articles.summary: The 10th Infantry Division has warned the public on AI-generated disinformation and manipulated content, emphasizing that official statements are communicated only through authorized channels

blocks.text: Claim: A photo shows the 10th Infantry (Agila) Division of the Philippine Army expressing support for Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC).

Why we fact-checked this: In the Facebook group “1st Infantry Tabak Division Philippine Army,” which has 22,900 members, the account “Regis Paller Enrique” posted a graphic allegedly showing personnel of the Philippine Army’s 10th Infantry Division (10ID) holding a banner with the text: “We support Senator Bato dela Rosa.”

The post has since been deleted, but the same graphic was reposted by at least five Facebook accounts in different groups, such as “The Best Ka Inday Sara,” “Rodante Marcoleta CDO Supporters” and “MAGSASAKA.” Membership in these groups ranges between 144,100 and 470,200.
The facts: In a statement on October 30, the 10ID said that the circulating graphic is AI-generated. The 10ID asserted that it does not subscribe to any political affiliation or preference.

The division wrote in its caption: “The 10ID upholds its commitment to professionalism, political neutrality, and service to the Filipino people, without political affiliation or preference. The Division stands firmly against disinformation and the misuse of artificial intelligence to misrepresent its personnel, emphasizing that its official positions and statements are communicated only through authorized channels.”
AI detection tools Sightengine and Hive Moderation flagged the circulating image as 99% likely to be AI-generated.

Bato in hiding: The AI-generated photo falsely attributed to the 10ID, which is headquartered in Davao de Oro, emerged after the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said it believes the senator is hiding in Mindanao under the protection of a “powerful armed group.” DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla, however, did not identify the alleged armed group.

Dela Rosa has a pending warrant of arrest issued by the ICC for his alleged role in former president Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs campaign. Since the shooting incident at the Senate last May 13, Dela Rosa has not been seen in public.
On October 23, Remulla said in a press conference that his department will offer a P50-million reward for those who can provide information that could lead to Dela Rosa’s arrest.
On November 9, the Philippine National Police said it received around 500 pieces of information on the senator’s possible whereabouts.
Previous fact-checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked claims involving Dela Rosa:

FACT CHECK: Bato dela Rosa not at recent INC rallies; post uses January 2025 video

blocks.text: – Jade Florido/Rappler.com
Jade Florido is a volunteer for Rappler’s Research and Data unit. She is a third-year Development Studies student at the University of the Philippines – Manila.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

blocks.text: Kraków shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say, as country mourns victims of attack
We are restarting our live coverage of European news after the mass shooting in Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, over the weekend in which six people were killed.
In an update this morning, the authorities said the 24-year-old Polish attacker, who had been injured in a shootout with police, has died in hospital.

Polish prosecutors had opened a terrorism investigation after the man, from the town of ‌Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski in ‌southeastern Poland, opened fire on Kraków’s popular Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon, killing six people, including a Briton, and injuring 17 others.

On the first of two days of national mourning declared after the rare mass shooting, police confirmed yesterday that three people found dead at the gunman’s home after the attack were his father, 53, mother, 52, and sister, 21.

blocks.caption: A woman lights a candle to commemorate the victims two days after the deadly shooting in Kraków, Poland. Photograph: Beata Zawrzel/AP

blocks.text: Five of the injured are foreign nationals from Britain, Austria, Germany, Portugal and Russia. Two police ⁠officers were also among the injured, one of whom was in a serious condition.
The interior minister, Marcin Kierwiński, said the suspect was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held “very radical” and “ultra-nationalistic” views.
But officials appeared to backtrack from these comments as nationalist opposition politicians questioned the grounds on which they were based.

“Until the matter is fully clarified and the authorities are in ‌possession of complete information, it is best to refrain from making comments, even if there are ​some initial indications,” government spokesperson Adam Szlapka told TVN24.

Meanwhile, the justice minister, Waldemar Zurek, said despite the attacker’s death, the investigation will continue, aiming to establish if he ⁠acted alone. Main Market Square reopened on Sunday evening after a security cordon was lifted.
Stay with us for the latest developments on the police investigation and other news from around the continent.

blocks.text: Kremlin denies that Europeans will participate in upcoming Abu Dhabi talks
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said some progress had been made on what the “security infrastructure” of Ukraine and Europe could look like after the war with Russia.

Rubio’s comments on Sunday come as Russia-Ukraine negotiations under US mediation have been set for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, with the talks expected to focus on postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts and steps to end the war.

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Trump’s son-in-law, will represent the US in Abu Dhabi. The Kremlin insisted this morning that no European ​officials will be there, rebuffing France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noel Barrot, who said French representatives would ‌be present.

In an interview ‌with CBS’s “60 Minutes” broadcast on Sunday, the US president, Donald Trump, said he believed the war would end ‌soon and suggested Ukraine could emerge from a settlement with altered borders. “I think we’re gonna have it done, and I think it’s gonna happen and they’re gonna end up with a little bit different shape Ukraine,” Trump said.

Despite Trump’s apparent optimism, no major breakthrough is expected at the talks as Vladimir Putin has consistently been sticking to his maximalist positions and both sides remain far apart, particularly on territory. But the US hopes the Russian president may be more willing to compromise after Trump struck ​a deal in October with the ⁠Kremlin to resume diesel exports to ​international markets.
A Ukrainian drone attack has hit Russia’s second-largest oil refinery in Kirishi, in the Leningrad region, the regional governor, Aleksandr Drozdenko, said.

A fire broke out at the refinery after the overnight Ukrainian drone strike, but has since been extinguished, he ​wrote on Telegram, adding that one ⁠woman had ​been killed ​by ​falling drone ​debris.
Ukraine has been targeting Russia’s oil industry, from pipelines ​and ports to refineries and tankers, in an effort to undermine ⁠Russia’s war economy.
The Kirishi refinery, about 800km (500 miles) from the Ukrainian border, has suffered several Ukrainian drone attacks ​this year.
The facility, one of the key suppliers of diesel to ​the domestic market and for export, is reported to produce more than 6% of Russia’s total refined oil.

articles.title: P6-M Matina property same as P10-M asset in Sara Duterte's SALN, Davao assessor says
articles.summary: The P6 million property in Matina, Davao City, that the prosecution in Vice President Sara Duterte"s impeachment trial alleged to have been left out of her statement of assets, liabilities, and net…

blocks.text: Published November 9, 2026 5:21pm

The P6 million property in Matina, Davao City that the prosecution in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial alleged to have been left out of her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN) is the same asset located in Barangay 74-A, worth P10 million, listed on the official’s SALN.
This was the testimony on Monday of Engineer Jaime Adalin, Davao’s city assessor, who was presented by the defense panel as its first witness on Day 40 of the impeachment trial.

Adalin answered in the affirmative when President Officer Senator-Judge Francis “Chiz” Escudero asked him if the property he and defense lawyer Atty. Lindon Bacquel had discussed at the start of the hearing was the same asset listed on the Vice President’s 2024 SALN.
The property listed on the SALN had an assessed value of P82,046 and a fair market value of P2,051,150. It is located in Barangay 74-A in Davao City.
How did he determine that the two properties were the same?
“It was based on the tax declaration that was presented a while ago… The tax declaration was cancelled after the sale,” Adalin said.
Escudero then asked why the SALN indicated a value of P10 million when the property’s deed of sale showed a purchase price of P6 million.
“I’m not actually aware, sir,” Adalin said.
Adalin also testified that Matina Crossing and Barangay 74-A were the same barangay.

“We inquired from our Comprehensive Land Use Plan… It says there Marina Crossing 74. And even in the barangay office themselves, there are pictures attached that show Barangay 74-A Matina Crossing,” Adalin said.
He said it was common knowledge in the area.
Bacquel ended his direct examination by asking Adalin if there was no truth to the prosecution’s allegation that the Vice President did not declare the property in her SALN.
The prosecution objected, and this was sustained by Escudero.

Prosecution witness Kathy Florence Baldonado of the Davao City Registry of Deeds testified on October 1 that, based on the deed of sale, there was no such property listed on Duterte’s SALN for the end of 2024.
The property was reportedly bought by Duterte's husband, Atty. Manases Carpio.
Escudero then said he looked into the SALN of the Vice President and did not find the property as one of the real properties declared .
Escudero, however, clarified that the SALN declaration has "limits."
Escudero said, referring to the Transfer Certificate of Title.
“The areas are too generic to identify and find out,” Escudero added. –Llanesca Panti/NB, GMA News

articles.title: Super El Niño may push power grids into red alerts, warns DOE
articles.summary: Extreme heat is expected to increase electricity demand while reducing power plant output.

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 5:10pm
The sun sets next to power lines along San Fernando town, Pampanga province, north of Manila on April 16, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines could face power shortages across all three major grids during the coming Super El Niño, with the Department of Energy warned.
Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said at a press briefing Monday, November 9, that higher temperatures could strain electricity supplies by reducing power plant output while driving up demand.
The government expects the El Niño to peak toward the end of 2026 and persist into early 2027.
Hydropower plants are expected to be the most affected, operating at only 40% capacity.
Solar plants, meanwhile, could see their output limited to around 80%. Coal, natural gas and oil-fired plants may also experience disruptions.
Garin said every 1-degree increase in temperature translates to an additional 100 megawatts in electricity demand.
Battery energy storage systems, which store electricity for dispatch when needed, currently add only 253 MW of capacity to support the country's power grids.
Red alerts possible in all 3 grids
Without additional intervention, the Visayas grid could experience around four red alerts, while Luzon and Mindanao could face one and two, respectively, according to the DOE's projections.
A red alert indicates that power supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the grid's required operating reserves, raising the risk of power interruptions.
Yellow alerts, which signal insufficient operating reserves, may also be raised as extreme temperatures put further pressure on generating facilities.

"Many of our plants are old, and many of our plants are non-compliant. When it's hot, they break down. Sometimes. there are unplanned outages because of things we don't have or weren't able to do. So, if you ask me, 'Will there be no plants that will go on unplanned outage? Are there any plants that will break down?,' we cannot assure that," Garin said.
DOE looks for backup power
The DOE is exploring additional generating capacity to reduce the risk of supply shortages.

"We're trying to find more barges to come in. It takes about three months for them to come in. We're coordinating with whoever has barges here in the country or deisel and coal plants on standby. We're doing our inventory and also preparing the private sector," Garin said.
She said the additional capacity would serve as a backup if actual supply conditions turn out worse than the department's projections.
Despite the risks, Garin sought to reassure the public, saying that "only the department needs to worry right now."
The Philippines remains under a state of national energy emergency over by conflict in the Middle East.
Higher energy costs helped push inflation to a three-year high in October and weighed on economic growth in the third quarter of 2026.
Dry conditions are also spreading across the country, with five provinces experiencing meteorological drought, 11 under dry spells and 10 reporting dry conditions.

articles.title: French police officers face trial over beating of black man not wearing mask during Covid
articles.summary:
Assault on Michel Zecler in 2020 is rare case of police brutality reaching court, at time of heightened tensions

Three French police officers are to go on trial over the beating of a black…

blocks.text: Three French police officers are to go on trial over the beating of a black music producer who they say was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic, in a rare case of police brutality reaching court.

The assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, triggered outrage in France over police violence, which victims and researchers say is systemic but authorities and law enforcement unions claim is limited to isolated cases.
“I expect this trial to hold the police officers accountable,” Zecler told Agence France-Presse in a recent interview.

Campaigners and rights groups have said the case was further evidence of what they saw as the French police’s systemic racism, in a country where they said ethnic minorities received harsher treatment than white people.

Police brutality has been in the spotlight during the student-led protests in recent weeks, during which a 14-year-old lost most of his teeth when a police officer appeared to fire a grenade at him at close range.
Police stopped Zecler outside his Paris studio on 21 November 2020, accusing him of failing to wear a mandatory face mask and suspecting him of cannabis use.
They pushed him into the entrance of his office and violently beat him in an assault recorded by his studio’s security cameras.

Police officers Aurelien B, now aged 29, Pierre P, 37, and Philippe T face charges of intentional violence committed in a group, as well as forgery when they tried to cover up their actions in an official report. They face up to 15 years in jail.
The officers’ lawyers declined to comment before the trial, which starts on Monday.

blocks.caption: Michel Zecler after the assault. Photograph: Hafida el Ali via AP

blocks.text: The producer sustained about 30 punches and truncheon blows to the face and body over a five-minute period, according to the investigation.
The medical report noted craniofacial trauma, a wound to the lip and scalp, and a complete rupture of his biceps tendon, leaving him unable to perform his job for 45 days.

France’s human rights ombudswoman has said police used “racist insults” during the assault, according to four witnesses. But the officers denied this and the alleged racism was not included in the indictment.
Zecler said they had used a racist slur against him. “I was insulted and I will repeat this at the hearing,” he said.

In their arrest report, the officers claimed the producer had hit them and tried to seize a truncheon, a version of events refuted by the camera footage that the French media website Loopsider released several days later.
after newsletter promotion
“I don’t understand the hatred I saw in their eyes,” said Zecler, who has a titanium anchor in his left arm after the ruptured tendon and says he still suffers nightmares.
“If there hadn’t been cameras … their reports would have been enough to send me to prison,” he said.
Most cases of alleged police brutality in France are dealt with internally.

A French police officer is to be tried over shooting dead 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk at point-blank range in June 2023 outside Paris. Video footage also contradicted the police’s version of events in that incident, sparking nationwide protests.
Guilty verdicts in alleged police brutality cases are rare.
In 2024, a judge gave suspended jail sentences to three officers who inflicted irreversible rectal injuries on a black man, Theo Luhaka, during a stop-and-search in 2017.

Young men “perceived as Arab, black or from north Africa” are four times more likely to be stopped by police than the rest of the population, according to a report last year by France’s rights ombudswoman.
They are 12 times more likely to be subjected to more severe measures, including being frisked during checks, it said after a survey of more than 5,000 people.
